_about: Permanent register of every published Briefings sector report. One entry per published sector — add an entry here when a sector's status in the AI Landscape sector-report-tracker.md moves to Published. The briefings.html page reads this file directly (no live feed, unlike the Practice Library — these are not Substack posts). 'image' is optional — a card thumbnail from the sector's Data Poster series (gold/Cormorant sub-brand); cards render fine without one.
_aboutCollaborations: Second, separate register for briefings co-authored with a named industry practitioner — same card fields as 'briefings' above, plus two more: 'collaboratorName' (required to trigger the byline) and 'collaboratorTitle' (optional, appended after a comma — e.g. 'Head of Claims Transformation, XYZ Insurance'). Rendered in its own Collaborations section on briefings.html with its own empty-state copy. Add an entry here, not to 'briefings', when a collaboration is published.

briefings.title: AI in UK Insurance Claims
briefings.standfirst: Claims costs are at record levels, the regulator has named claims handling its top priority for 2026, and the first AI-fabricated claims are already on the record.
briefings.imageAlt: The first mover on AI in UK claims wasn't the insurer — 95% of insurers already use AI, 46% report only partial understanding, £174m in fraud cases combatted

briefings.title: AI in UK Social Housing
briefings.standfirst: Awaab's Law starts a legal clock the moment a landlord becomes aware of a hazard. The regulator, the Ombudsman and the sector's own flagship AI case study all say the constraint is data, not technology.
briefings.imageAlt: It doesn't ask what you fixed, it asks what you knew — 30 Nov Awaab's Law Phase 2, +43% Ombudsman property-condition findings, 31% of staff using AI vs 22% given access

briefings.title: AI in UK Energy Retail
briefings.standfirst: Satisfaction is at a record high and complaints at their lowest since 2022, while debt hits £4.79bn and arrears without a repayment plan run at three times managed debt. Ofgem has twice this year found the customer record itself unreliable — and that record is what an AI system would learn from.
briefings.humanMoment: Self-disconnection on a smart prepayment meter
briefings.imageAlt: Every service measure is improving. Every measure of debt is getting worse — 82% satisfaction, £4.79bn debt and arrears, 48% Ombudsman signposting rate

briefings.title: AI in UK Grocery Retail
briefings.standfirst: Four regulators hold a position on AI in or around this sector and none is aimed at its largest deployments. Facial recognition is reaching around two hundred stores on the strength of a two-store trial, while machine learning forecasting already sits inside a statutory duty requiring due care, consultation and an explainable basis.
briefings.humanMoment: The tap on the shoulder at the self-checkout
briefings.imageAlt: Every regulator has a position. None of them is aimed here — five ICO priorities with retail not among them, zero mentions of technology or AI across two 2026 Groceries Code Adjudicator publications, and Sainsbury's facial recognition going from two stores to around two hundred

collaborations.title: When the Model Said It Was Fine
collaborations.standfirst: The US has just excluded agentic AI from its flagship model risk framework. European supervisors have answered by restating the frameworks they already have. A joint examination of the discipline financial services built to govern models — and why, on its own terms, it no longer reaches what AI now deploys.
collaborations.humanMoment: The named signature on the annual MRM attestation
